semantics.note: Faithful. Keeps 'exponentially higher' and the consumer-setting scope. 'Less tolerable' partly reads as the speaker's own judgment.

contract.note: Reading 'exponentially' as 'substantially greater' is ordinary and fair. Taking the comparison as workplace/RPA tasks fits the UiPath context, but the speaker never stated a baseline, so the result turns on the evaluator's choice.

evidence.note: OSWorld, April 2024: best agent at about 12% success versus humans at about 72%. Supports 'error-prone' only. There is no consumer-vs-workplace comparison and no tolerance data.
WorkArena, March 2024, which is outside the target month. Shows enterprise agents also fell short. Not a matched comparison.

reviews.rationale: The error-prone part is supported by e1. The core comparison (substantially higher failure risk and lower tolerance in consumer settings) has no matched evidence in the packet, and e2 hints that workplace agents also failed. The claim as a whole is not settled.

contract.note: Requiring evidence that links Altman's expertise, and named mathematical or physical limits, to problems that persist is a fair, ordinary reading.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own 2023 disclosure: GPT-4 still hallucinates, with some reduction. Says nothing about cause or Altman.
Proves a statistical lower bound on hallucination for some facts and says other errors can be mitigated. Partial and conditional; no link to Altman.
April 2026 reporting that Altman lacks deep technical expertise. Undated recollections; does not show that this caused the limitations.

reviews.rationale: Nothing in the packet connects Altman's expertise to the persistence of the problems. The mathematical evidence covers only one narrow class of hallucinations, and no physical limit is identified. Neither causal link is established or refuted.

evidence.note: First-hand fxguide account from April 2024: the same prompt gave different results, details were inconsistent, and only about 1 in 300 of the footage was used. It also documents a finished film, which limits the claim.

reviews.rationale: The contemporaneous filmmaker account shows that requested content and continuity were unreliable, and that the film needed heavy retries, selection and correction. That meets the support condition for the preview period.

contract.note: Defining 'kind of useful' as a practical contribution to a finished production matches the low bar the speaker set. Marking the condition 'met' is odd for a necessity claim, but the result does not depend on it.

evidence.note: Company/PR disclosure of the June 2024 Toys R Us film: shows practical use, with heavy iteration and corrective VFX. No measurements show whether any prerequisite was missing.
OpenAI's own December 2024 release notes admit many limitations. Not a measurement of any particular useful deployment.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given, and the early-resolution rule is not met: no evidence shows a useful deployment that lacked one of the three prerequisites. The Toys R Us film is a self-promotional company disclosure with no matched measurements.
